summary: Simple, fast retrieval-augmented generation that builds a knowledge graph from your documents, with a server and web UI.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LightRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system from HKU. It extracts entities and relationships from your documents into a knowledge graph and uses it with vector search to answer questions, through a Python library or a server with a web UI and REST API.
sixtySeconds.problem: Plain vector RAG can miss how facts connect. LightRAG adds graph-based retrieval while staying simple and fast, and it now also parses multimodal content.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a well-known, MIT-licensed graph RAG system with a prebuilt web UI, many storage backends and per-role LLM settings.
requirements: An OpenAI API key or another OpenAI-compatible provider for the LLM and embeddings

overview: Install the server with uv tool install "lightrag-hku[api]" (the PyPI package includes the WebUI), copy env.example to .env, set LLM_BINDING_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_BINDING_API_KEY, and run lightrag-server.
The WebUI is at http://localhost:9621/webui and the API docs at /docs. For other providers, set the binding host and model values too.
Security warning from the README: the server binds to all interfaces with authentication off by default, so secure it before running on a shared network or cloud host. LightRAG is MIT licensed.
limitations: Needs LLM and embedding API usage to index
Server is open by default; you must secure it

troubleshooting.solution: It binds to 0.0.0.0 with auth off by default; secure it before exposing it.
Also set LLM_BINDING_HOST, LLM_MODEL, EMBEDDING_BINDING_HOST and EMBEDDING_MODEL.
